static_traits.name: He Jialin
static_traits.family_status: Father was a mechanic; other details not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with other musicians strained by negative self-evaluation; has a few musician friends, but has not yet discussed career insecurity with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar problems appeared before; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, able to self-reflect; steady (neutral) tone; thinking prone to comparison, tending to ignore positive evidence, with black-and-white self-evaluation

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling trapped in current music work, believing one's skills are insufficient and unable to do other jobs; worsening daily when seeing other musicians succeed, gradually feeling despair about changing careers.
basic_info.core_demands: Feeling despair about career prospects, hoping to explore other options through counseling and gain more realistic self-evaluation and perspective.
growth_experiences: About two years after starting the same music job, gradually formed the self-evaluation of 'not skilled enough' through frequent comparison with same-age, more successful musicians; although there were occasional successes (completing difficult pieces or receiving positive feedback), positive experiences were quickly overshadowed by self-doubt and pressure about the next challenge, accumulating over time into feelings of being trapped and helpless.

core_beliefs: I am a person without ability / not skilled enough
I am not as good as same-age musicians

special_situations.event: Seeing same-age, more successful musicians' updates and achievements online (social media)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach their level or have not kept improving, it means I am not good enough and am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing, increasing self-pressure; avoiding discussing insecurity with friends to prevent being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never succeed like her;I am not good enough

special_situations.event: After a performance, receives positive feedback or successfully completes a difficult piece
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only constantly achieving more can prove I am capable; one success does not mean I am really good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Quickly shifting attention to inadequacies and the next challenge, spending less time on positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count for anything; I am still not good enough

special_situations.event: Interacting with other musicians offline, seeing their career leaps like awards/signings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my career has not risen noticeably, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying silent in social settings, sharing less career insecurity, avoiding comparison
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; my career is stagnating

special_situations.event: Thinking about whether to switch careers or explore other career paths
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not highly skilled, I cannot do any other work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintaining the status quo, not proactively exploring new options to avoid failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too unskilled, I cannot do anything else

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and to have one's ability seen, expecting to have autonomy in choosing and developing a career
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying about being humiliated in comparison, being seen as 'not good enough'
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being evaluated by devaluing oneself and avoiding exposing vulnerability
Maintaining surface distance in peer relationships to preserve a sense of safety
Pressuring oneself with higher standards to gain control and avoid anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough failure easily defeated by comparison

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor affirms one's achievements or invites one to stay with positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client views positive evidence as 'insufficient to prove ability', measuring oneself by extreme standards (transference: internalizing external high standards as the sole criterion)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keep a gentle tone, mainly inquiring; invite stating both successes and inadequacies, helping see gray areas and both sides.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Situations discussing other musicians' success or interacting with peers
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning jealousy of others and anxiety into self-blame, believing 'it is all because I am not good enough' (self-deprecation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain empathy and acceptance, name the self-attack pattern, guide turning comparison into concrete actionable goals rather than wholesale negation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing industry standards and the belief that one 'must keep improving'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Taking others'/the industry's high standards as the sole basis of self-worth in an undigested way
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses a clarifying and distinguishing tone, explores their personal values and choices, encourages setting feasible standards and pace of their own.

manifestations: Subjectively experiences 'being trapped in the current job', lacking a sense of control over career choice
Tying self-worth to external success standards, feeling unable to autonomously define 'good enough'
outcomes: Decreased drive, actions to explore new careers blocked

manifestations: Having friends but not yet discussing career insecurity, tending to bear comparison and self-doubt alone
outcomes: Social support not yet utilized, relationship tension
Intensified self-criticism, increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes the industry's high standards as the only basis for self-worth
Language and thinking showing the absolutist rule of 'if not constantly progressing, it is failure'
Positive feedback seen as 'insufficient to prove ability'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Being cautious yet harsh in self-evaluation during sessions, emphasizing inadequacies over achievements
Rarely discussing insecurity with friends, worrying about being judged
Relationships with peers strained by negative self-evaluation

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing other musicians succeed or making comparisons, the client usually engages in self-deprecation, feeling helpless and avoiding exploring new career options.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On receiving positive feedback from the audience/peers after a performance, the client at that moment felt pride and relief, experiencing a moment of 'being able to do it', and negative self-evaluation was temporarily weakened.
exception_events.reason: Different support: receiving external positive feedback; different understanding: briefly focusing attention on actual performance and achievements rather than comparison.

exception_events.target_problem: When facing highly difficult tasks, the client usually worries about failure and engages in self-denial with 'I am not skilled enough', leading to decreased drive.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When successfully completing a difficult piece once, the client experienced competence and control, emotions shifting from anxiety to confidence and satisfaction, briefly breaking the old self-doubt cycle.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: fully practicing and preparing the piece; different understanding: treating the success experience as evidence of ability (rather than immediately negating it).

positive_force: Having certain musical skills and experience, able to complete difficult pieces and receive positive feedback
Willing to seek counseling and try recording and affirming one's own achievements
Has a few peer friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Excessively compares with others and relies on external validation to determine self-worth
Black-and-white self-evaluation and negating positive evidence
Catastrophizing and helplessness intensifying the constrained experience of career choices
Avoiding discussing insecurity with friends, social support not yet fully utilized

target_behavior.behavior: Persistently comparing with other musicians and engaging in self-deprecating negative self-talk
antecedent: Seeing same-age musicians' successful social-media updates
Interacts with peers offline, hears of others winning awards or signing contracts
When thinking about career change and new options
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by the introjected rule 'if not constantly progressing, it equals failure' and external-validation orientation, forming the core belief 'I am not skilled enough / not as good as others'
target_behavior.function: Avoids the risk of failure and being evaluated, maintaining temporary control and safety
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance and decreased drive; relationship tension with peers; blocked exploration of career change, worsening subjective helplessness and despair

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding discussing career insecurity with friends
antecedent: Situations requiring discussing career insecurity or seeking support
When feeling shame and inferiority after comparisons
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying that exposing vulnerability will be negated or humiliated, turning anxiety into self-blame for self-protection
target_behavior.function: Avoiding judgment and embarrassment, reducing anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet utilized, increased sense of isolation and negative self-evaluation, relationships further strained
